questions.question: What is the key difference between shadow mode and canary rollout?
options: Shadow mode uses 1% of traffic while canary uses 10%
Shadow mode duplicates production requests with zero user impact; canary shifts live user traffic progressively
Shadow mode only tests latency while canary tests output quality
Shadow mode requires feature flags while canary uses DNS-based traffic splitting
questions.explanation: Shadow mode duplicates real production requests to the candidate model, logs results, and compares — with zero user impact. Canary routes a percentage of live users to the new model. Shadow catches distribution issues; canary exposes users to the actual product change.

questions.question: What is the standard canary traffic progression for LLM rollouts?
questions.explanation: The lesson specifies: 1% → 10% → 25% → 50% → 75% → 100% with quality gates at each step. The slow progression at low percentages catches regressions early when blast radius is minimal.

questions.question: Up to what percentage run-to-run accuracy variation can occur on identical LLM inputs due to GPU non-determinism?
questions.explanation: The lesson cites up to 15% run-to-run variance on identical inputs due to GPU FP non-associativity (floating-point reduction order varies by batch) and batch-size variance. This means 'stable' in an LLM canary must account for inherent non-determinism.

questions.question: What is the rollback strategy that takes seconds rather than hours?
options: Re-deploy the previous Docker image from the container registry
Flip the policy feature flag and revert the pinned model digest in the registry
Drain the current replica set and scale up the previous replica set
Run a database migration to restore the previous model configuration
questions.explanation: The lesson's rollback recipe: policy lives in a feature flag (flip percentage in config, takes seconds) + model is pinned to a registry digest. Rollback = revert flag + set digest to previous. No redeploy required. Rollbacks that require redeploy take 10-30 minutes.

questions.question: The lesson names five LLM-specific canary metrics to track. Which of the following is NOT one of the five?
questions.explanation: The five canary metrics are: latency percentiles, cost/request, error/refusal rate, output length distribution, and user feedback rate. GPU utilization is an infrastructure metric, not one of the five LLM-specific quality gates.

questions.question: Why is cost described as a variable in LLM canary rollouts rather than a constant?
options: Provider pricing changes frequently and can shift during a rollout
A 20% better model can be 3x more expensive per call, so quality improvements may not be free
Cost varies by region and the canary may serve different geographies
Caching behavior differs between models, making cost unpredictable
questions.explanation: The lesson warns: a new model that is 20% better on quality benchmarks may cost 3x more per API call. Teams that approve rollouts based only on quality metrics without monitoring cost/request can inadvertently triple their inference bill.
